title: Corner entanglement scaling with projected entangled pair states
authors: Chloé Van Bastelaere, Rui-Zhen Huang, Laurens Vanderstraeten
abstract: Entanglement scaling provides a powerful probe of universal properties at quantum critical points. In two dimensions, contributions originating from a corner-shaped bipartition exhibit a universal scaling, which is determined by the underlying conformal field theory. We develop a method to extract this corner entanglement entropy from projected entangled pair states directly in the thermodynamic limit. When applied to models at a quantum critical point, we show that the corner contribution exhibits scaling with the effective correlation length, in agreement with the hypothesis of finite-entanglement scaling. Our results for the corner coefficients are consistent with other methods, demonstrating the efficiency of our method for diagnosing strongly-correlated quantum critical points in two dimensions.
summary: This work introduces a robust tensor network method to calculate the corner entanglement entropy in 2D quantum systems. By analyzing the scaling of this corner contribution, the authors successfully extract universal critical coefficients for models like the TFIM and XY model. This provides a powerful diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum critical points in strongly correlated matter.
main_problem: The paper develops a method to extract the universal scaling of the corner entanglement entropy from Projected Entangled Pair States (PEPS) directly in the thermodynamic limit for 2D systems.
main_result: The corner entanglement contribution scales logarithmically with the effective correlation length ($\xi$) at quantum critical points, yielding consistent corner coefficients ($c_2$) when applied to the TFIM and XY models.
method: The authors use the PEPS formalism to calculate the Rényi-2 entropy ($S_2$) for corner-shaped bipartitions, separating the result into an area law term and a corner contribution ($S_{c,2}$).
model_or_system: The study applies to critical 2D quantum models, including the Transverse Field Ising Model (TFIM) and the Bilayer XY Model, and also tests universality using the classical 3D Ising Model.
key_observables: Corner entanglement entropy ($S_{c, 2}$), Area law prefactor ($a_2$), Correlation length ($\xi$), and the corner coefficient ($c_2$).
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the thermodynamic limit and the scaling behavior with the correlation length $\xi$.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the hypothesis of finite-entanglement scaling for PEPS simulations and approximates the infinite system using boundary MPS techniques.
figures_summary: Figures show the scaling of the area law prefactor ($a_2$) and the corner contribution ($S_{c,2}$) versus the bond dimension ($\chi$) for the 2D TFIM and Bilayer XY model, demonstrating the extraction of $c_2$.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the theoretical framework for calculating entanglement entropy in PEPS, extending the analysis from linear to corner bipartitions. It then applies this method to calculate $c_2$ for various critical models, comparing results across different systems and methods.
why_interesting: The rigorous extraction of universal critical exponents like $c_2$ using tensor networks provides a powerful, non-perturbative diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum critical points in strongly correlated materials.
